newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs jump late to new highs, pork bellies fall.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs jump late to new highs, pork bellies fall.

text.p: CME hog futures ran up again late and posted new contract highs in June through October before ending strong. Pork bellies tumbled at the close after a late rally failed, traders said.

Lean hogs closed mostly 0.825 to 0.025 cent per lb higher with February up 0.225 at 77.175 cents. June set a new high of 81.400 cents. Pork bellies fell to end mixed, 0.600 cent lower to 0.575 higher with February off 0.550 at 80.550 cents.
Rolling of long positions into April kept February under pressure, but all months moved up late as renewed fund buying and local short covering hit buy stops, traders said.

Expectations of tight hog runs and higher cash prices Tuesday, partly from weather-reduced runs, boosted futures. Continued effects of the last USDA Hogs and Pigs report again lifted back months to new highs, they said.
"Our last Hog and Pig report is telling us that there is no reason with the numbers to be bearish, at least for the first three quarters of the year," said Don Roose, President U.S. Commodities Inc.
"Out here (Iowa), demand still seems to be solid and the numbers seem to be falling fairly close to the report," Roose added.

ABN Chicogo Corp, Prudential Securities and Refco bought April and sold February early before buying by Lind-Waldock supported February late. Mixed fund buying offset selling by Rand Financials and R.J. O'Brien in April, pit sources said.

In hog options, ADM Investor Services bought February 78 calls and sold 76 puts early while commission houses bought April 80 calls and sold June 76 puts. A large local spread long June 75 put/short 76 put, pit sources added.
Pork belly futures rallied late along with values in other livestock pits, and then tumbled in the last few minutes of trade as long liquidation pushed prices down into sell stops, traders said.

A strong cash belly market quoted at noon provided late support but futures appeared overbought and turned down, especially considering they hold a large premium to cash belly prices ahead of February becoming the spot position next week, they said.
"How much are you going to let February bellies stretch out from cash," Roose noted.
Funds were on both sides of the market late. E.D.&F. Man bought before selling by Iowa Grain turned prices lower, pit sources said. ((Jerry Bieszk 312-408-8725))
